verses.text: The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah the son of Shobal became the father of Jahath; and Jahath became the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These are the families of the Zorathites.
These were the sons of the father of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. The name of their sister was Hazzelelponi.
Penuel was the father of Gedor and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah.
The sons of Helah were Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
Hakkoz became the father of Anub, Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.
Jabez was more honorable than his brothers. His mother named him Jabez,  saying, “Because I bore him with sorrow.”

Jabez called on the God  of Israel, saying, “Oh that you would bless me indeed, and enlarge my border! May your hand be with me, and may you keep me from evil, that I may not cause pain!” God granted him that which he requested.
Chelub the brother of Shuhah became the father of Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.
Eshton became the father of Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Ir Nahash. These are the men of Recah.
The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. The sons of Othniel: Hathath.
Meonothai became the father of Ophrah: and Seraiah became the father of Joab the father of Ge Harashim; for they were craftsmen.
The sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam. The son of Elah: Kenaz.
The sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon; and she bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.
His wife the Jewess bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. These are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered took.
The sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, were the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Ishi: Zoheth, and Ben Zoheth.
The sons of Shelah the son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of those who worked fine linen, of the house of Ashbea;
and Jokim, and the men of Cozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who had dominion in Moab, and Jashubilehem. These records are ancient.
These were the potters, and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah: they lived there with the king for his work.
The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul;
Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, and Mishma his son.
The sons of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brothers didn’t have many children, and all their family did not multiply like the children of Judah.
They lived at Beersheba, Moladah, Hazarshual,
at Bilhah, at Ezem, at Tolad,
at Bethuel, at Hormah, at Ziklag,
at Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, at Beth Biri, and at Shaaraim. These were their cities until David’s reign.
Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan, five cities;
and all their villages that were around the same cities, to Baal. These were their settlements, and they have their genealogy.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah the son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu the son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
and Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah —
these mentioned by name were princes in their families. Their fathers’ houses increased greatly.
They went to the entrance of Gedor, even to the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.
They found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceful; for those who lived there before were descended from Ham.

These written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and struck their tents. The Meunim who were found there, and they destroyed them utterly to this day, and lived in their place; because there was pasture there for their flocks.
Some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to Mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
They struck the remnant of the Amalekites who escaped, and have lived there to this day.

footnotes.content: Here begin the sons of Judah—Perez, Hezron, and the rest who carry forward the tribe's name and calling. These names mark the long line that leads, generations down, to David and then to the Messiah himself. The Lord doesn't forget a name or a promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Reaiah and his descendants settle in Zorah, building families and homes in the Promised Land. Each generation inherits not just a name but a calling to dwell where the Lord has placed them. Faithfulness often looks like simply staying, tending what God has given.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Among the sons of Etam, note Jezreel and Idbash—and their sister Hazzelelponi, whose name means 'shade of my eye.' Even in a genealogy, she is named and remembered, valued by her household. The Lord sees the quiet ones, the ones who tend home and heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Penuel and Ezer—sons of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah—are the fathers of Gedor and Hushah. Yet there is another Hur remembered here: the one who held up Moses' arms at Rephidim. Through generations, God weaves together families and faithfulness. Bethlehem itself is called Ephrath elsewhere in Scripture, a place the Lord would hold dear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ashhur and his two wives, Helah and Naarah, remind us that ancient life was complex—plural marriages existed in those days, though not without their own sorrows and tensions. The Lord met people where they stood and has never stopped doing so.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Naarah bore four sons: Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari—each one a blessing in her household. She is remembered by name and by her fruit. A mother's faithfulness in raising children echoes through generations, even when the world forgets her.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Helah's three sons—Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan—are named and recorded, part of the great tapestry God is weaving. Each name, each life, matters in His sight, whether or not we remember them thousands of years later.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hakkoz fathered Anub and Zobebah, and Aharhel through them. Again the genealogy records how the covenant people multiply and fill the land, each generation extending the promise. The Lord honors fruitfulness and presence in the land He gave.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jabez was more honorable than his brothers—a stunning phrase that breaks through dry genealogy. His mother named him 'Jabez' meaning 'sorrow' because his birth brought her pain. Yet he did not remain defined by that sorrow. Sometimes our deepest wounds become the soil from which our greatest faith grows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jabez cried out to God: 'Bless me and enlarge my border. Let your hand be with me, and keep me from evil.' God answered. Here is bold prayer—not for riches or fame, but for blessing, for room to grow, for God's presence, and for protection from wrongdoing. The Lord delights when His children ask such things of Him, and He grants them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chelub, the brother of Shuhah, fathered Mehir, who fathered Eshton. The record continues, generation layered upon generation. Each link in the chain was a person who lived, loved, and built their own small corner of the great inheritance God was giving His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eshton became father to cities—Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. The men of Recah built places, established settlements, created homes where the covenant people could dwell and flourish. Building and settling are acts of faith in the Lord's promises.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Kenaz are recorded: Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel himself was a judge of Israel, known for his courage and his devotion to the Lord—and his family line carries that faithful witness into generations yet to come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seraiah became the father of Joab, father of the inhabitants of 'Ge Harashim'—the Valley of Craftsmen. They were artisans, workers of fine skill. The Lord honors honest work and skillful hands; He sees the carpenter, the weaver, the builder as much as the king and priest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh—this is Caleb the faithful spy, the one who stood with Joshua and believed the Lord's promise even when others doubted. His line continues, and his descendants inherit the blessing that flows from his faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Jehallelel—Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel—each one named, each one part of the covenant people. The Lord's attention is not too small for the quiet branches of the family tree.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ezrah fathered Jether and others through his wife, who bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah. Women who are named and honored for their fruitfulness remind us that the Lord values mothers and daughters as surely as sons.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mered married Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh—a remarkable bridge between Egypt and Israel. She bore his children and gave them inheritance in the land of promise. Love and faithfulness sometimes cross borders the world would keep separate.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wife of Hodiah—sister of Naham—fathered Keilah and Eshtemoa. Again, women appear in these genealogies, not merely as objects but as bearers and builders of the covenant line. Their names and work matter to the Lord's story.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Shimon—Amnon, Rinnah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Ishi—Zoheth and Ben Zoheth. Each line continues, each branch bears fruit. The Lord's covenant people grow and multiply, filling the land as He commanded.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Shelah include Er, Laadah, and the families of those who worked fine linen. Craftspeople, artisans, and workers are named and honored here—their callings and their handiwork matter in God's sight as much as any crown.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and Saraph—'these records are ancient.' The chronicler pauses to remind us that he is passing down an old memory, a lineage traced back through ages. What we inherit from faithful generations shapes what we pass on.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The potters of Netaim and Gederah lived and worked for the king. Their hands shaped clay; their labor served the kingdom. Even humble craftspeople—especially humble craftspeople—are part of God's design for order and flourishing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the sons of Simeon are recorded: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul. One of the twelve tribes steps into view, their lineage preserved and honored. The Lord's covenant was made with all Israel; all are remembered in His sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shallum, Mibsam, and Mishma—each son, each generation passing the name and blessing forward. Genealogies like this show us that the Lord builds His kingdom not through great events alone, but through the faithful, ordinary lives of His people across generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Mishma—Hammuel, Zaccur, Shimei. The line continues unbroken, each name a link in the chain the Lord is forging. Nothing that matters to God is ever forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, yet his brothers did not multiply as much—nor did their families grow as large as Judah's. Here the chronicler notes a difference: some branches flourish more than others, yet all are counted among God's people. Fruitfulness is a blessing the Lord sovereignly bestows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They dwelt at Beersheba, Moladah, Hazarshual—the places Simeon's people made their homes. Geography marks where faith took root, where families built their altars and their fields. The land itself becomes part of the covenant story.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad—more settlements of Simeon's line, each one a place where God's people dwelt and worshiped. The Lord's covenant people were not meant to be wanderers forever; they were called to possess and dwell in the land He promised.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag—these cities housed the families of Simeon. Each place remembered, each settlement a sign that the Lord was fulfilling His promise to His people. They went from slavery to inheritance, from wandering to home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri, Shaaraim—these cities belonged to Simeon 'until the reign of David.' The chronicler marks a turning point: the land was theirs to dwell in, and then a great king arose to unite the kingdom. The Lord works through time and through chosen leaders.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Five more settlements—Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, Ashan. The chronicler is thorough in listing Simeon's possession, reminding every generation where their inheritance lay. The Lord's faithfulness is specific and particular, not vague.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All their villages around the same cities extended to Baal. These were their settlements, and they had their genealogy—their place in the great record of God's covenant people. The Lord sees us not as isolated individuals but as part of a great family, woven into His eternal purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah—leaders of Simeon in a later age are named and honored. They too are part of the sacred record, remembered for their role in shepherding God's people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joel and others of Simeon's leaders are listed—Jehu, Joshibiah, Seraiah, Asiel. Each man named for his faithfulness and leadership. The Lord raises up shepherds for His flock in every generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah—a full roster of leaders and faithful ones. Their names are preserved because they mattered to God and to His people in their time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ziza and his lineage—Shiphi, Allon, Jedaiah, Shimri, Shemaiah—are traced back through time. Here is continuity, a family line rooted deep in the history of God's people. Each name honors those who came before.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: These men, mentioned by name, were princes in their families; their fathers' houses increased greatly. Leadership and blessing go together—as the Lord raises up shepherds, His people flourish. The growth of their families was itself a sign of God's favor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They journeyed to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley, seeking pasture for their flocks. The people of Simeon were shepherds—they followed their herds to greener ground, always trusting God to provide. Sometimes faithfulness means simply going where the Lord leads.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They found good pasture—fat and abundant—and the land was wide, quiet, and peaceful. Those who had lived there before were descendants of Ham. The Lord gave them what they sought, and they dwelt in peace. His provision is both generous and good.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the days of Hezekiah, these men struck the tents of the Meunim and destroyed them utterly, taking their place for pasture. The chronicler dates the event to a specific king—history is woven through the reign of known rulers. God's providence moves through the lives of both great and small, and all serve His purposes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Five hundred of Simeon's sons, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, went to Mount Seir. They traveled far to secure their inheritance, led by men of courage and faithfulness. The Lord equips His people with leaders for the work they must do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They struck the remnant of the Amalekites who escaped, and dwelt there to this day. Readers today hear an echo of God's faithfulness through all generations—the battles His people fought, the land they claimed, the legacy they built. We too inherit a story of deliverance and are called to faithfulness in our own time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
